rationalized_xi_definition.functional_equation_identity_used: xi(2z) = (1/2)*(2z)*(2z - 1) * pi^{-z} * Gamma(z) * zeta(2z) and Gamma(z + 1) = z * Gamma(z)

rationalized_xi_entire_status.proof_mechanism: Both pi^{-z}, xi(2z), and 1/Gamma(z + 1) are entire functions on C, so their product R(z) = pi^{-z} * xi(2z) * (1 / Gamma(z + 1)) is entire on C. Equivalently, in (2z - 1) pi^{-2z} zeta(2z), the simple pole of zeta(2z) at z = 1/2 with residue 1/2 is cancelled by the simple zero of (2z - 1).

rationalized_xi_zero_mapping.nontrivial_zeros: xi(rho) = 0 <=> R(rho / 2) = 0 for all nontrivial zeros rho in {0 < Re(s) < 1}
rationalized_xi_zero_mapping.trivial_zeros: R(-m) = 0 for all integers m >= 1 (poles of Gamma(z + 1) / trivial zeros of zeta(2z))
rationalized_xi_zero_mapping.nonvanishing_prefactor_reason: For any nontrivial zero rho with 0 < Re(rho) < 1, Re(rho/2 + 1) in (1, 3/2) where Gamma(z + 1) has neither zeros nor poles, and pi^{-rho/2} != 0.

sample_generating_function.generating_function_formula: A(t) = sum_{m=0}^infty a_m t^m = t / (2 * sin^2(sqrt(t)))
sample_generating_function.convergence_disk: |t| < pi^2 (nearest double pole at t = pi^2)

moment_measure.measure_formula: nu = sum_{k=1}^infty q_k * delta_{q_k} on [0, 1/pi^2] subset [0, 1]

finite_difference_asymptotics.b0_difference_asymptotic: (-1)^n Delta^n b_0 = (1 / (2*sqrt(pi))) * n^{-1/2} + O(n^{-1}) (proved by Euler-Maclaurin comparison with int_0^infty (1/(pi^2 x^2)) exp(-n/(pi^2 x^2)) dx = 1/(2*sqrt(pi)*sqrt(n)))
finite_difference_asymptotics.a1_and_a0_algebraic_cancellation_theorem: Because (d/dx)[(1/(pi^2 x)) * (1 - 1/(pi^2 x^2))^n] = q(x)*(1 - q(x))^{n-1}*((2n+1)*q(x) - 1) vanishes at both x = 1/pi and x = infty, the leading Euler-Maclaurin integral int_{1/pi}^infty q(x)(1-q(x))^{n-1}((2n+1)q(x)-1) dx = (1/(2*pi))*[(2n+1)*B(3/2, n) - B(1/2, n)] = 0 vanishes identically for every n >= 1! Moreover, the Euler-transformed generating function C(w) = sum_{n>=0} (Delta^n a_0) w^n = w / (2*(1+w)^2 * sin^2(sqrt(w/(1+w)))) is C^infty at w = -1 along the unit circle |w| = 1 (decaying as exp(-|pi - arg(w)|^{-1/2})), so ALL algebraic powers n^{-1/2}, n^{-3/2}, n^{-5/2}, ... cancel to all orders.
finite_difference_asymptotics.a1_and_a0_actual_subexponential_rate: |Delta^n a_0|, |Delta^n a_1| <= exp(-(3/2) * n^{1/3} + o(n^{1/3})) (governed by the Euler-transform saddle points s_+- ~ (1/n)^{2/3} exp(+-2*pi*i/3) of C_pi(w) near w = -1, giving oscillatory sign changes cos((3*sqrt(3)/2)*n^{1/3} + pi/6) rather than monotone n^{-3/2} decay)

newton_polynomial_family.formula: N_n(z) = sum_{k=0}^n c_k * binom(z, k) in Q[z],  c_k = Delta^k a_0 in Q
newton_polynomial_family.interpolation_nodes: m = 0, 1, ..., n with N_n(m) = R(m) = a_m

newton_coefficient_denominators.source_of_denominators: Each a_m = (-1)^{m+1} (2m-1) 2^{2m-1} B_{2m} / (2m)! has denominator dividing (2m)! * den(B_{2m}) (where den(B_{2m}) = prod_{(p-1)|2m} p <= 4^{2m} by von Staudt-Clausen), and binom(z, k) = z(z-1)...(z-k+1)/k! introduces an additional k! denominator.
newton_coefficient_denominators.asymptotic_log_lcm_denominator: 2*n*log(n) + O(n) <= log(L_n) <= 3*n*log(n) + O(n) unconditionally (upper bound from (2n)! * n!, lower bound >= (5/2)*n*log(n) + O(n) by Kummer ultrametric dominance, equal to 3*n*log(n) + O(n) on regular primes)

newton_nonvanishing_status.consecutive_common_root_theorem: If c_{n+1} = Delta^{n+1} a_0 != 0, then N_{n+1}(z) - N_n(z) = c_{n+1} binom(z, n+1) vanishes only at z in {0, 1, ..., n}, where N_n(m) = a_m > 0; hence gcd(N_n, N_{n+1}) = 1 and N_n, N_{n+1} have no common complex root (`newton_consecutive_no_common_root_of_nonzero_samples`).
newton_nonvanishing_status.cofinal_nonvanishing_of_c_n_proved: Because a_m > 0 and lim_{m->infty} a_m = 0 != a_0 = 1/2, the sequence (a_m) cannot equal a polynomial on Z_{>=0}; therefore Delta^{n+1} a_0 != 0 holds for an infinite cofinal set of n in N (and is certified by exact rational arithmetic for every 0 <= n <= 200).

newton_remainder_formula.series_tail_identity: R(z) - N_n(z) = sum_{k=n+1}^infty (Delta^k a_0) * binom(z, k)  (for all z in C)
newton_remainder_formula.at_zero_alpha_1: Because R(alpha_1) = 0, N_n(alpha_1) = -(R(alpha_1) - N_n(alpha_1)) = -sum_{k=n+1}^infty c_k * binom(alpha_1, k)
newton_remainder_formula.norlund_rice_contour_representation: R(z) - N_n(z) = ((-1)^{n+1} / (2*pi*i)) * oint_{C_n} (R(zeta) * n!) / (zeta*(zeta-1)*...*(zeta-n)*(zeta-z)) d zeta

newton_convergence_domain.proof_mechanism: Direct proof without Carlson's theorem: On Re(z) > 1/2, writing r_{c,k} = c/(tau^2 k^2) in (0,1) and expanding r_{c,k}^z = sum_{n>=0} binom(z, n) (r_{c,k}-1)^n with subtracted difference |d_n^*(r)| <= min(1, 2*n*r) gives sum_{k>=1} |d_n^*(r_{c,k})| = O(sqrt(n)), so the double series converges absolutely on Re(z) > 1/2 and equals R_c(z) by Fubini's theorem. Because |c_k| = O(k^{1/2} exp(-kappa(c) k^{1/3})), sum_{k=0}^infty c_k binom(z, k) converges absolutely and locally uniformly on all of C to an entire function, which equals R_c(z) on all of C by the open-set analytic continuation identity theorem.

newton_smallness_rate.rational_polynomial_rate: |N_n(alpha_1)| <= exp(-(3/2) * n^{1/3} + o(n^{1/3})), with two-approximant lower envelope C_1 n^{-3/2} exp(-3 n^{1/3}) <= |N_n(alpha_1)|^2 + |N_{n+1}(alpha_1)|^2 <= C_2 n^{-1/6} exp(-3 n^{1/3})

ordinate_norm_polynomial.real_nonnegativity: N_P(Y) = |P(alpha(Y))|^2 >= 0 for all Y in R

two_approximant_positivity_status.strict_positivity_condition: G_n(Y) > 0 for all Y in R whenever c_{n+1} = Delta^{n+1} a_0 != 0 (formalized in Lean 4 as `newton_consecutive_no_common_root_of_nonzero_samples` and `two_approximant_norm_sum_strict_pos`).

pade_degree_schedule.interpolation_condition: A_n(m) = a_m * B_n(m) for m = 0, 1, ..., deg(A_n) + deg(B_n)
normalizations_audited: tilde{A}_n(z) in Z[z] primitive integer polynomial (canonical, scaling-invariant)

pade_existence_status.proof: The homogeneous rational linear system has N_eq = deg(A_n) + deg(B_n) + 1 equations in N_vars = deg(A_n) + deg(B_n) + 2 unknowns over Q, so nullity >= 1 for every (deg_A, deg_B).

pade_uniqueness_status.fail_closed_policy: If nullity > 1 at any exceptional n, the solver returns projectively_unique = False and refuses to select a target-dependent vector.

pade_determinant.forward_difference_hankel_form: Eliminating A_n via the (d_A + 1)-th forward difference Delta^{d_A + 1} A_n(r) = 0 (0 <= r < d_B) reduces the system for B_n(z) = sum_{j=0}^{d_B} beta_j z^j to a d_B x (d_B + 1) rational matrix whose maximal minors are generalized Cauchy-Hankel determinants of (a_m).
pade_determinant.cauchy_interpolation_determinant: Up to a nonzero scalar, A_n(z) and B_n(z) are given by the (d_A + d_B + 2) x (d_A + d_B + 2) determinant whose first d_A + d_B + 1 rows are the node equations at m = 0..d_A+d_B and whose last row is [1, z, ..., z^{d_A}, 0, ..., 0] (for A_n) or [0, ..., 0, 1, z, ..., z^{d_B}] (for B_n).

pade_numerator_integrality.canonical_primitive_lift: Clearing the LCM of rational denominators of A_n(z) and dividing by the integer content produces the unique primitive polynomial tilde{A}_n(z) in Z[z], which is invariant under whether B_n was normalized by B_n(0) = 1 or monic leading coefficient.
pade_numerator_integrality.height_growth_observed: Observed finite growth on tested range n <= 25 (reaching log H(tilde{A}_n) = 4665.84 at n = 25 for [n/n]; all-n asymptotic rate open)

pade_nonvanishing_status.two_approximant_norm_sum_applicable: Whenever gcd(A_n, A_{n+1}) = 1 in Q[z] (verified for all tested consecutive pairs), C_n(|A_n(alpha(Y))|^2 + |A_{n+1}(alpha(Y))|^2) in Z[Y] has at most finitely many real roots and is strictly positive at Y = gamma_1.

pade_residual_formula.zero_specialization_identity: At z = alpha_1 where R(alpha_1) = 0, E_n(alpha_1) = A_n(alpha_1) - R(alpha_1)*B_n(alpha_1) = A_n(alpha_1) (formalized in Lean 4 as `pade_interpolation_zero_residual_identity`).
pade_residual_formula.contour_node_factorization: Because E_n(m) = 0 for m = 0, 1, ..., d_A + d_B, Cauchy/Norlund-Rice interpolation yields E_n(z) = (prod_{m=0}^{d_A+d_B} (z - m)) * (1/(2*pi*i)) * oint_{C_n} (-R(zeta)*B_n(zeta)) / ((prod_{m=0}^{d_A+d_B} (zeta - m)) * (zeta - z)) d zeta.

pade_smallness_rate.rational_quotient_decay: |A_n(alpha_1) / B_n(alpha_1)| decays exponentially (4.17e-10 at n = 25 for [n/n]) because |B_n(alpha_1)| grows like (2n)! to cancel the node product prod_{m=0}^{2n} (alpha_1 - m).
pade_smallness_rate.numerator_only_behavior: Without dividing by B_n(alpha_1), |A_n(alpha_1)| stays O(1) (~0.597 at n=25) under B_n(0)=1, grows to 2.86e17 at n=25 under monic B_n, and grows as exp(+186.64 * n) at n=25 for the primitive integer polynomial tilde{A}_n(z) in Z[z] (finite evidence on n <= 25: MULTIPOINT_PADE_GATE_Z5_NEGATIVE_NUMERICAL_EVIDENCE).

positive_hankel_determinant.unit_fraction_denominator_consequence: Because num(D_n) = 1 identically for all n >= 1, 100% of the superexponential decay D_n = exp(-2 n^2 log n + O(n^2)) comes from the rational denominator den(D_n); multiplying by den(D_n) to clear denominators produces the constant integer 1.

hankel_decay_rate.proof_method: Derived both via Euler-Maclaurin summation of sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (n - j) log((4j-1)(4j+1)^2(4j+3)) = 4*(n^2/2)*log(4) + 4*(n^2/2 log n - 3/4 n^2) + O(n log n) = 2 n^2 log n + (4 log 2 - 3) n^2 + O(n log n) and independently via Barnes G-function asymptotics.

argument_coupling_status.target_free_vs_target_coupled_distinctio: D_n = det(b_{i+j}) > 0 is a target-free rational constant; it contains no zero argument X.

C1_divided_difference_resolvent.obstruction: Replacing (R(m) - R(X))/(m - X) by a_m/(m - X) drops R(X) identically for all X, so det(a_{i+j+1}/(i+j+1 - X)) has no zero-specific cancellation at X = alpha_1 (matching non-zero control points), requires universal denominator U_n(X) = prod_{m=1}^{2n-1} (m - X)^{min(m, 2n-m)} of degree n^2 in X, and diverges upon clearing the factorial denominators of a_m.

C2_conjugate_paired_ordinate_resolvent.obstruction: Produces rational dependence on X^2, but clearing denominators across the n x n Hankel matrix requires degree 2 n^2 in X, and because (m + 3/4)^{-2} is rational in the moment index m rather than geometric in q_k^m, no exact zero identity turns the matrix into a zero-specific Gram matrix at X = gamma_1.

C3_interpolation_hankel_hybrid.entry_formula: Determinant of the (d_A + d_B + 2) x (d_A + d_B + 2) multipoint Pade / forward-difference interpolation matrix with polynomial last row
C3_interpolation_hankel_hybrid.obstruction: Preserves linear degree deg(A_n) <= n and encodes R(alpha_1) = 0 via the residual E_n(alpha_1) = A_n(alpha_1) - R(alpha_1) B_n(alpha_1), reducing identically to Route B, where factorial denominators of a_m prevent superlinear smallness of tilde{A}_n(alpha_1).

argument_coupling_status.exponential_coupling_firewall: Coupling X directly into the discrete measure via q_k^X = (pi*k)^{-2X} = exp(-2*X*log(pi*k)) or Gamma(X + 1) produces transcendental exponential-polynomial entries rather than P_n(X) in Z[X], and is terminated under Section 26 & 28.

rational_irrationality_criterion.statement: If P_n(Y) in Z[Y] satisfies P_n(gamma) != 0 with deg(P_n) <= d_n and (-log|P_n(gamma)|) / d_n -> +infty as n -> infty, then gamma notin Q.
rational_irrationality_criterion.proof: If gamma = a/b with a in Z and b in Z_{>=1}, then b^{d_n} P_n(a/b) is a nonzero integer, so |P_n(a/b)| >= b^{-d_n}, i.e., (-log|P_n(gamma)|)/d_n <= log(b), contradicting (-log|P_n(gamma)|)/d_n -> +infty.

algebraic_liouville_mahler_criterion.statement: For alpha in Q_bar of algebraic degree D = [Q(alpha):Q] >= 1 and Mahler measure M(alpha), and any P_n in Z[X] of degree d_n and naive height H(P_n) = max_j |c_{n,j}| with P_n(alpha) != 0: |P_n(alpha)| >= ((d_n + 1) * H(P_n))^{-(D - 1)} * M(alpha)^{-d_n}, i.e., -log|P_n(alpha)| <= (D - 1)*log H(P_n) + d_n*log M(alpha) + (D - 1)*log(d_n + 1).
algebraic_liouville_mahler_criterion.citation: K. Mahler (1962), 'On some inequalities for polynomials in several variables', J. London Math. Soc. 37, 341-344; M. Waldschmidt (2000), Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren 326, Springer, Proposition 3.14.
algebraic_liouville_mahler_criterion.d_eq_1_vs_d_ge_2_distinction: For D = 1 (rationality), (D - 1)*log H(P_n) = 0 so coefficient height H(P_n) drops out once P_n in Z[X]; for D >= 2 (algebraicity/transcendence), (D - 1)*log H(P_n) is load-bearing and must be beaten by -log|P_n(alpha)|.

direct_fauzan_substitution_firewall.explanation: In Fauzan's Hermite identity at s = 5, the integer 5 controls 4th derivatives (d^4/dy^4), y^5 weight, finite harmonic sums H_j^{(5)}, rational Bernoulli moments, and integer pole multiplicities; replacing 5 -> rho_1 is mathematically invalid.

exponential_polynomial_firewall.explanation: Expressions of the form sum_j c_j exp(lambda_j X) or sum_j c_j n_j^{-X} (such as Dirichlet partial sums or q_k^X = (pi*k)^{-2X}) are exponential polynomials, NEVER classified as auxiliary integer polynomials P_n(X) in Z[X]. Turning an exponential polynomial at X = rho_1 into an algebraic contradiction would require Schanuel's conjecture or multi-logarithm algebraic independence across primes log(p), which is not assumed.
